newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to launch global image-building campaign.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to launch global image-building campaign.

text.p: Sri Lanka will launch a global public relations campaign next month to attract investors and tourists by playing down a 13-year-old war with separatist Tamil rebels.
A Tourist Board official told Reuters on Friday that the government selected New York-based Manning Selvage and Lee to run the $2.5 million-campaign to improve the Indian Ocean island's image abroad.

"It is going to be a concerted PR exercise where we will demonstrate that Sri Lanka still remains a great place for tourism, for investment and for business," said the official, who declined to be identified.
Sri Lanka has been plagued by negative publicity from fighting between its armed forces and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.

The LTTE want an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, but the LTTE says the toll is higher.

The government says the war is largely contained in the north and the east and is away from the financial centres and tourist attractions such as the southern beaches, the central hills and the ancient kingdoms in the north-central region.
The rebels have not attacked tourist targets so far but have also not hesitated to hit those related to the economy.

In January last year, a suspected LTTE suicide bomber rammed a truck loaded with explosives into the Central Bank building in downtown Colombo, killing 100 people and destroying a section of the city's financial district.
